title: Treatment Effect Estimation with Adjustment Feature Selection

problem.claim: Treatment effect estimation requires selecting observed covariates as adjustment features.

gap.claim: Empirical treatment effect estimation performance varies substantially with different extra variables beyond confounders.

narrative_sequence.summary: Adjustment features are selected from observed covariates for treatment effect estimation.
Real-world data may include treatment-only and outcome-only variables in addition to confounders.
Unbiased estimation is achieved in principle when all confounders are included among the adjustment features.
Different extra variables can nevertheless produce substantially different empirical estimation performance.
Variable separation and selection have received growing attention when instrumental and precision variables are present.

source_observation.claim: Including all confounders is theoretically sufficient for unbiased treatment effect estimation, but extra variables can affect empirical performance.

interpretation.claim: Adjustment-feature selection may matter even when confounding control is theoretically satisfied.

application.claim: Evaluate adjustment-feature choices separately from confounder coverage in empirical treatment effect analyses.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not specify which feature-selection strategy performs best or under what data conditions.

unknowns: The proposed method or algorithm is not specified.
No experiments, datasets, numerical results, or comparisons are supplied.
The conditions under which extra variables change estimation performance are not specified.
